texts: mixed: the generic rule itself is right (every Keeper gets a using-the-crowd-rule event, and it fires), but "for generations" cannot ride it — a generic sentence hands every atom to each individual Keeper, so the span comes out as "each Keeper used the crowd rule for at least two generations", which the sentence never claims; the span belongs to the practice across Keepers and there is no carrier for that, so it has to be dropped and the content is lost either way. Give the span its own finite clause with a singular subject so it attaches to the practice rather than to each Keeper: "Keepers use the crowd rule, and this practice has continued for generations."
